key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produced denser, harder Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings with 27% lower sliding wear volume than conventional APS, but little improvement in normal-impact erosion.
engineering_relevance: HV-APS is promising for Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings on steel components exposed to sliding wear, though its advantage depends on the wear mode.
method: Sprayed Metco 5241 powder onto S235 steel using radial-feed conventional APS and axial-feed supersonic HV-APS.
Compared coating microstructure, phase transformations, porosity, and microhardness.
Evaluated erosion at 90° impact and ball-on-disc sliding wear under a 30 N load.
evidence_signal: Compared with APS, HV-APS reduced porosity from 11.99% to 6.16%, increased hardness from 897 to 1141 HV0.2, and reduced wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm³; erosion rates remained close at 0.20 versus 0.19 mg/g.
watch_item: The comparison changes both torch technology and powder-feed geometry, so improvements cannot be attributed to axial feeding alone.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
